decision.title: Decimal arithmetic over libmpdec (packet )
decision.summary: Decimal arithmetic wraps vendored mpdecimal 4.0.1 in sxml_decimal, with the allocator scope in the patched mpalloc.c, a per-heap digit limit, exact sums and products, and 34-digit quotients.

item.p: Vendoring: mpdecimal 4.0.1 (third_party/mpdecimal.version), libmpdec only; patches marked "sxml patch" in mpalloc.c, mpdecimal.h and context.c. The configuration is chosen in mpdecimal.h from the width of size_t (CONFIG_64 or CONFIG_32 with the portable ANSI arithmetic, __uint128_t under GCC and Clang), so one header serves every target, 32-bit WebAssembly included; no MASM or inline assembler. WASI has no signal.h: the never-called trap handler does nothing there.

Scope location: the thread-local lives in the patched mpalloc.c, not in src/, so libmpdec does not depend on the sxml library that links it; src/decimal.c sets it with mpd_sxml_exchange_allocator_scope. Shrinking a block keeps it (never fails); growth is allocate, copy, release ().

Value type: sxml_decimal wraps an mpd_t with a static struct and a dynamic coefficient: movable byte for byte, made by the functions that write it, released by sxml_decimal_finalize without a scope. No create/destroy: cells (1.7) embed it.

Limits and precision: a configuration (allocator, maximum_digit_count default 10000, division_digit_count default 34) per item heap. Sums, differences, products, idiv and mod are exact or SXML_STATUS_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (FOAR0002); quotients are computed to max(34, digits of both operands) significant digits, half to even (op-numeric-dividepint2args-5 then gives its second allowed result). Division by zero is SXML_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT (callers raise FOAR0001).

Binary floating point: casting uses the shortest round-trip decimal (0.1e0 gives 0.1, as XPath processors do); fn:atomic-equal and numeric comparison use the exact value. Decimal to double/float goes through strtod/strtof on text without a decimal point (locale-free), 780 digits plus a sticky digit, so rounding is exact.
Size: a stripped wasm32-wasip1 program using parse, divide, shortest conversion, canonical text and to_double grows by 89 KB (35 KB gzip) over one using only the allocator.
